reviews.comment: Unfortunately, I think this guy died. He was saving us from Supreme Leader Teizer and his totalitarian rule over PHYS 222. Now, we have nobody to save us from the Teizer rein of terror
Schuessler wants everyone to get an A. This is not an easy class don't expect it to come natural to you. Go to the review session practice old exams if possible and you'll be fine.
Dr. Schuessler is the better prof for 222. Although the lectures are not very helpful, the TA is beneficial during reviews and the exams look like the homework problems.

He is very up there in age, so his lectures were not very meaningful. He just reread the slides every time and there was an attendance question per lecture relating to a concept from the slides. However, the exams were fairly easy, you just need to study the slides and homework to do well. Cannot thank the TA enough for making this course doable.

I think he cares about his students and genuinely enjoys teaching, but all his lectures were just reading off his slides. The TA carried the class in teaching, but Dr.Schuessler was very funny and cared for his students.

Honestly, he's a chill guy. Very tenured and knows his stuff but not a great lecturer. Pretty easy class though. Tests are multiple choice and he gives extra credit. Definitely better than the other options for this class.

Never went to class a single time except for the first day of semester and got A. If you have him for 222 instead of Teizer, you're lucky. You'll pretty much learn nothing but it will be the easiest A you can ever get in college. Take his class before he retires!

Can't even put into words how bad this experience was. Professor has little awareness for what is going on in class, and barely says a few words as he skips through most slides and ends class an hour early. (Who would have thought that spending 5 seconds on each slide leads to class only lasting 15 minutes with 0 learning effect.) TA was great tho.

He was a very incoherent lecturer, did not teach well at all and did not solve problems with the class. He is a very sweet and kind man, but the lectures didn't teach me much at all. The homework was upwards of 3 hours a week and did not reflect anything useful for the test.

Dr. Schuessler is awesome. His lectures can be a bit boring but he adds lots of examples and personal experience. Homework is easy and grading is lenient and he has lots of extra credit. Getting an A is easy if you take notes and put in a bit of effort.

I'm lucky I knew at least part of this class from a previous semester or I would've had to drop it again. The only reason people showed up to class was to get the password for the attendance quizzes. Go to SI+recitation, and find the google drive of old tests to study. Hw is annoying, but ig has to be done. Most of class was handled by the TA

He is the very definition of mid, lectures are useful, and somewhat interesting talking about his past experiences. If you have to take Physics 1 at A&M I'd say, take Hans if you don't have a spot in Igor's, Kelly's, or Ford's class.

Hans is a nice dude and has had a great career in physics research, but he's not a good professor for Physics 1 at this point. He is not good with technology and mainly just clicks through the slides without much elaboration. Most people skipped his lectures as they were not useful. Take physics 1 at community college its garbo at TAMU.

Professor Schuessler is a very sweet man, but not a good professor. He doesn't teach at all, so you'll have to teach yourself. Not only does he just click through slides, he even skips some. Lectures were so ill attended (because everyone decided they were worthless) that our TA started offering extra credit for showing up. Utilize SI sessions.

The only reason you need to go to lectures is the quizzes given at the end of class. It is much more beneficial to learn the material yourself from the textbook rather than trying to learn from the lecture. He never works out any examples, just shows them on the screen worked out. The content is hard, but the exams are very easy in comparison.

Hes an OG physicist. Hell tell you stories about the times hes met all the scientists that the book talks about. He cares deeply about his students and puts effort into his class. His lectures can be hard to follow but you are supposed to read the corresponding chapter before class. If you do that, you will gain a lot from his lectures.

Going to class is an absolute waste of time, basically had to teach myself everything. Due to the fact there are only 20 multiple choice questions on the exams , the way its structured sets you up to fail. Failing even one question takes you down 5 points with no partial credit whatsoever. Take this class when he isnt teaching it.

Dr. Schuessler is a very smart man and I'm sure he is a talented researcher as well. However this does not translate into his lectures. The class felt like a waste of 75 minutes. Lectures were slow, boring and dry, tests and homework had multiple, severe typos, and as a result, attendance went down sharply as the semester progressed.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I haven't learned a thing in his class. The only reason I didn't give him a 1 is because his exams are exactly like the homework, so if you can do that, you'll get an A on the exams.

Basically physics at A&M sucks. The tests are common exams so you may or may not have been taught what is on the exam. The homework does not really help prepare you for the exams either. You can make an A in lab, recitation, and homework and still get 30's on the exams. I suggest you take physics at a community college.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough
